name: Christian Heresiarchs and Dissenting Movements
note: Hub collective for intra-Christian heterodox figures and movements condemned by the ecumenical councils; modern category attested throughout Pelikan and Lambert.

name: Arius
note: Alexandrian presbyter (c.256-336) whose teaching that the Son was created and subordinate to the Father was condemned at Nicaea (325); attested in Athanasius, Socrates Scholasticus, and Pelikan.

name: Nestorius
note: Patriarch of Constantinople (c.386-450) condemned at Ephesus (431) for teaching two distinct persons in Christ and rejecting Theotokos; attested in Pelikan.

name: Pelagius
note: British ascetic (c.354-418) who denied original sin's bondage of the will, condemned at Carthage (418) and Ephesus (431); chief antagonist of Augustine, attested in Pelikan.

name: Donatus Magnus
note: Bishop of Carthage (d. c.355) and eponym of the Donatist schism over the validity of sacraments administered by traditores; attested in Pelikan.

name: Montanus
note: 2nd-c. Phrygian founder of the New Prophecy (Montanism), an ecstatic prophetic movement condemned for novel revelation; attested in Eusebius and Pelikan.

name: Priscillian
note: Bishop of Avila (d. 385), ascetic teacher executed for heresy/sorcery, first Christian put to death by the state for heterodoxy; attested in Sulpicius Severus and Pelikan.

name: Eutyches
note: Constantinopolitan archimandrite (c.380-456) whose teaching of a single divine nature in Christ was condemned at Chalcedon (451); attested in Pelikan.

name: Sabellius
note: Early 3rd-c. teacher of modalist monarchianism (the Father, Son, and Spirit as modes of one person), eponym of Sabellianism; attested in Hippolytus and Pelikan.

name: The Bogomils
note: 10th-c. Balkan dualist movement founded under the priest Bogomil rejecting the material order and ecclesiastical hierarchy; transmitter of dualism westward, attested in Lambert.

name: The Cathar Perfecti (Albigensians)
note: The consoled elect of the Cathar/Albigensian dualist church of Languedoc and Lombardy (12th-13th c.), suppressed in the Albigensian Crusade; attested in Lambert.

name: The Paulicians
note: 7th-9th c. Armenian/Byzantine dualist sect rejecting the material world, the Old Testament, and church sacraments; precursor in the dualist transmission to the Bogomils, attested in Lambert.

name: Peter Waldo
note: Lyon merchant (c.1140-c.1205) who founded the Waldensian movement of apostolic poverty and unauthorized lay preaching, condemned 1184; attested in Lambert.

name: The Waldensians
note: The Poor of Lyon, an evangelical dissenting movement of vernacular preaching and biblicism founded by Peter Waldo, surviving into the Reformation; attested in Lambert.

name: The Bosnian Church
note: Medieval autonomous Bosnian church (13th-15th c.) long associated with dualist/Bogomil influence and condemned as heretical by both Rome and Constantinople; attested in Lambert.
